title: How do we write four folds short, and what is five to the power four?
description: Four folds of the sheet are written in short as a power of two, and five to the power four is found by multiplying four fives step by step. Keeko's doubt is that five to the power four is five times four.
teaching_notes: One idea: an exponent counts how many times the base is multiplied by itself, so a repeated multiplication has a short form. Watch for students who read five to the power four as five times four.

source: Write the thickness after 4 folds as a power of 2, and find
video_script.why: The child has doubled the thickness fold by fold and now learns the short way to write a number multiplied by itself again and again.
video_script.substitution: The book's own four folds, written as zero point zero zero one times two to the power four, and the book's five to the power four.
video_script.anchor: a chain of repeated multiplications on the board, drawn first for the four folds of the sheet and then for fives
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads five to the power four as five times four, which is repeated adding. The exponent counts how many fives are multiplied together.
video_script.payoff_line: Five to the power four is six hundred twenty five

final_answer.value: 0.001 × 2⁴ cm, which is 0.016 cm; 5⁴ is 625 with base 5 and exponent 4
final_answer.spoken: zero point zero zero one times two to the power four centimetres, which is zero point zero one six centimetres, and five to the power four is six hundred twenty five, with base five and exponent four

maths_rules: in 5⁴ the base is 5 and the exponent is 4
video_script.design: One idea: the exponent counts the equal factors. The chain of equal factors stays all video; base and exponent are named once, in the ground; one slip at the end.

beats.on_screen: title card, From your book; the sheet folded four times with 0.001 cm × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 written, and 5 to the power 4 in a box beside it

marks.book: the title card From your book arrives
marks.fold: the sheet is folded four times and the chain of twos is written
marks.ask: five to the power four is written in a box beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the folded sheet.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>A sheet is folded four times, and each fold doubles its thickness.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we write that thickness in a short way, and what is five to the power four?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 2 × 2 × 2 is written as 2³; the repeated 2 is circled and labelled base, the small 3 is circled and labelled exponent

marks.base: the repeated 2 is circled and named base
marks.exp: the small 3 is circled and named exponent

narration: <bookmark mark='chain'/>When one number is multiplied by itself again and again, we write it in a short way.
<bookmark mark='base'/>The number that is repeated is called the base.
<bookmark mark='exp'/>The count of how many times it is repeated is called the exponent.

beats.on_screen: Given: thickness 0.001 cm; 4 folds, each fold doubles it; the number 5 to the power 4

marks.given: the thickness, the four folds and five to the power four are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a sheet zero point zero zero one centimetres thick is folded four times.

beats.on_screen: To find: thickness after 4 folds as a power of 2; value of 5⁴; its base and exponent

marks.find: the three things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write the thickness as a power of two.
We also find five to the power four, with its base and exponent.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, four folds double the thickness four times, so multiply by two, four times.
<bookmark mark='short'/>In short, that is zero point zero zero one times two to the power four centimetres.

marks.two: 5⁴ is written out as four 5s multiplied

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, five to the power four means four fives multiplied together.
Write it as five times five times five times five.

marks.next: 25 × 5 = 125 is written, then 125 × 5 with the result left open

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, multiply two at a time.
Five times five is twenty five.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Twenty five times five is one hundred twenty five, and one more multiplication by five is left.

marks.four: the 5 is labelled base and the 4 is labelled exponent

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, name the parts of five to the power four.
The base is five, and the exponent is four.

marks.a2: 5⁴ = 625 is boxed with its base and exponent

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>After four folds, the thickness is zero point zero zero one times two to the power four centimetres.
That is zero point zero one six centimetres.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Five to the power four is six hundred twenty five.
Its base is five, and its exponent is four.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the chain of fives
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 5 × 4 = 20 appears, then is crossed out; four fives multiplied together are drawn in a row

marks.fix: 5 × 4 = 20 is crossed out and four fives joined by multiplication are drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks five to the power four is five times four, which is twenty.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the exponent counts how many fives are multiplied together.
Four fives multiplied is not the same as four fives added.
